key_insight: Jointly tuning reward-shaping parameters and DQN hyperparameters with Bayesian optimization helps overcome common reinforcement-learning failure modes in autonomous parking.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that reward design and algorithm settings must be co-optimized to obtain reliable, smooth non-holonomic control in real vehicle-parking applications.
method: Parameterized reward shaping with coverage-gated alignment feedback
Drive-direction switch regularization and aligned episode termination
Surrogate-based Bayesian optimization for joint meta-optimization of reward and DQN hyperparameters
evidence_signal: On an autonomous parallel parking task, the co-optimized DQN improved success rate and trajectory smoothness compared with uncalibrated baselines.
watch_item: The approach may require task-specific reward engineering and expensive joint tuning, which can limit portability to new environments.
paper_title: Optimal Reward Shaping: Autonomous Car Parking Case Study
